gotcha: bullmq Worker.close() waits for active jobs and never resolves while Redis is unreachable, so a process that awaits it on SIGTERM never exits; race it against a timeout and call close(true) to force it.
bullmq needs maxRetriesPerRequest set to null on the ioredis connection used by a Worker; with the ioredis default the worker throws when it starts.
bullmq repeatable jobs are keyed by name and repeat options; changing the cron pattern adds a second schedule instead of replacing the old one, so remove the old repeatable job first.
bullmq removes completed jobs only when removeOnComplete is set; without it every finished job stays in Redis and memory grows until the instance runs out.
With maxRetriesPerRequest set to null, ioredis queues commands until the connection returns, so an HTTP handler can hang; keep a finite value outside of queue workers.
ioredis with lazyConnect stays disconnected until the first command or an explicit connect(); health checks that only read the status field report it as down.

Prisma Client keeps a connection pool per instance; creating a new PrismaClient on every request or hot reload exhausts database connections, so reuse one instance stored on globalThis in development.
prisma migrate dev can reset the database when it detects drift; never point it at a shared or production database and use prisma migrate deploy there.
Prisma returns BigInt for BIGINT columns and JSON.stringify throws on BigInt values; convert them to strings or numbers before sending a response.
Prisma interactive transactions time out after five seconds by default; long work inside $transaction fails with a transaction already closed error unless the timeout option is raised.
drizzle-kit generate writes migration SQL and a snapshot in drizzle/meta/*.json; deleting a SQL file without its snapshot entry makes the next generate repeat or skip changes.
drizzle-orm returns timestamp columns as Date objects by default; mode string keeps the database text, which avoids time zone shifts for date-only values.
next 15 no longer caches fetch requests by default in the app router; set cache to force-cache or revalidate explicitly where caching is wanted.
Next.js inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_ environment variables at build time; changing them in the runtime environment has no effect until the app is rebuilt.
In the next app router, a component that uses useState or useEffect needs the use client directive at the top of its file, otherwise the build fails with a server component error.
next/image needs remotePatterns for external image hosts; an image from an unlisted host fails with a 400 error from the image optimizer.
React 18 StrictMode mounts, unmounts and mounts components again in development, so effects run twice; make effects idempotent and clean up subscriptions instead of guarding them with a ref.
A React state update with the same object reference does not re-render; mutating an array and setting it again shows stale UI, so copy it before the update.
Keys in a React list must be stable; using the array index as key mixes up input state when items are inserted or reordered.
Vite exposes only variables prefixed with VITE_ to client code through import.meta.env; other variables are undefined in the browser by design.
The vite dev server pre-bundles dependencies into its cache; after linking a local package or switching branches, stale optimized deps load two copies of React until the server restarts with --force.
Vite serves the public folder at the root path; referencing a public asset with a /public prefix works in dev but breaks in the production build.
vitest runs test files in parallel worker threads; tests that share one database or port interfere unless the file runs sequentially or each worker gets its own resource.
vi.mock calls are hoisted to the top of the file, so variables defined in the test file are not available inside the mock factory unless they come from vi.hoisted.
jest fake timers do not advance promises; after jest.advanceTimersByTime a pending promise chain still needs the microtask queue flushed before the assertions run.
jest picks the jsdom or node test environment from its config; code that touches window fails under the node environment unless the file declares the jsdom environment.
Express 4 does not catch rejected promises from async route handlers; the request hangs unless the error is passed to next or a wrapper is used, while Express 5 handles them.
express.json() only parses requests with a JSON content type; a client sending text/plain gets an empty req.body and no error.
Express error middleware must declare four parameters; a handler with three arguments is treated as normal middleware and never receives the error.
fastify serializes replies with the response JSON Schema; properties missing from the response schema are silently dropped from the reply.
Fastify plugins are encapsulated; a decorator or hook registered inside a plugin is invisible to sibling plugins unless the plugin is wrapped with fastify-plugin.
zod object schemas strip unknown keys by default; use passthrough or strict when unknown fields must be kept or rejected.
z.coerce.number() turns an empty string into 0 instead of failing, so optional numeric form fields need a preprocess step that maps empty strings to undefined.
Tailwind generates only the classes it finds as complete strings in content files; class names built by string concatenation are missing from the CSS.
Tailwind CSS 4 moves configuration into CSS with the theme directive and an import of tailwindcss; a tailwind.config.js file is ignored unless it is loaded with the config directive.
TypeScript type-only imports are erased; with isolatedModules a re-export of a type needs export type, otherwise transpilers emit an import of a value that does not exist.
TypeScript paths in tsconfig only affect type checking; the runtime or bundler needs its own alias configuration, or imports fail with module not found.
With moduleResolution node16 or nodenext, relative imports in ESM TypeScript need the .js extension even though the source file ends in .ts.
ESLint 9 reads only the flat config file eslint.config.js by default; an old eslintrc file is ignored without a warning unless the legacy mode is switched on.
nx caches task outputs by their inputs; a script that reads an environment variable not declared in the target inputs replays a stale cached result.
The nx daemon keeps the project graph in memory; after adding a project or changing tsconfig paths, run nx reset if commands still use the old graph.
bun test runs every test file in a single process, so module-level state and mocks leak between files unless they are reset in afterEach.
Bun loads .env files automatically, but a variable already set in the shell wins over the file, which surprises scripts that expect the file to take precedence.
In graphql-js, a resolver that returns null for a non-null field turns the nearest nullable parent into null with an error, so missing data removes more of the response than expected.
Pothos builder types are declared once in the SchemaTypes generic; a scalar that is not registered there makes its field types fall back to unknown.
The Pothos Prisma plugin selects only the relations a query asks for; resolving a relation through the plain Prisma client inside a field bypasses this and causes N+1 queries.
excalibur ships its type definitions under node_modules/excalibur/build/dist/*.d.ts; read them for the installed version instead of the online docs, which follow the latest release.
In excalibur, actors added to a scene do not run onInitialize until the scene is activated, so code that reads their graphics in the constructor sees nothing.
SQLAlchemy async sessions do not lazy-load relationships; accessing an unloaded attribute raises MissingGreenlet, so load relations with selectinload in the query.
SQLAlchemy sessions expire objects on commit by default; reading an attribute after commit triggers a new query, or fails once the session is closed, unless expire_on_commit is false.
Pydantic v2 replaced dict() and parse_obj with model_dump and model_validate; the old names still work with deprecation warnings but behave differently for aliases.
Pydantic v2 treats an Optional field without a default as required; give such fields an explicit default of None when they may be omitted.
FastAPI runs plain def endpoints in a thread pool and async def endpoints on the event loop; a blocking call inside an async def endpoint stalls every request.
FastAPI caches dependencies per request; the same dependency used twice runs once unless use_cache is set to False in Depends.
pytest fixtures with session scope are created once per worker under pytest-xdist, not once per run; shared setup like a database must handle several workers.
pytest collects classes named Test only when they have no __init__ method; a test class with __init__ is skipped with nothing more than a warning.
Docker sends the whole build context unless .dockerignore excludes it; without the file node_modules and .git are uploaded, builds slow down and secrets can end up in layers.
Each RUN line in a Dockerfile creates a layer; deleting files in a later RUN does not shrink the image, so clean caches in the same RUN that created them.
nginx proxy_pass with a trailing slash replaces the matched location prefix, while without it the full URI is passed; a missing slash sends wrong paths to the backend.
nginx buffers proxied responses by default, which delays server-sent events and streaming responses; set proxy_buffering off for those locations.
Celery acknowledges a task before it runs by default; a worker killed in the middle of a task loses it unless acks_late is enabled and the task is idempotent.
Celery serializes task arguments with JSON by default; passing ORM objects or datetimes without converting them fails or delivers strings.
alembic autogenerate does not detect renamed columns or tables; it emits a drop and an add, which loses data unless the migration is edited by hand.
Django QuerySets are lazy and cache their results; iterating the same queryset twice reuses them, but slicing it or calling all() again runs a new query.
With DEBUG on, Django stores every SQL query in connection.queries, so long-running management commands leak memory unless DEBUG is off.
Node.js does not exit while an open handle such as a timer, socket or database pool remains; a test or script that never closes its pool hangs at the end.
In Node ESM modules __dirname and require are not defined; use import.meta.dirname on recent versions or fileURLToPath of import.meta.url.
Node fetch has no default timeout; a request to an unresponsive server waits until the socket gives up, so pass AbortSignal.timeout to every call.
Redis KEYS blocks the server while it walks every key; use SCAN with a cursor in production code.
Redis drops the expiry of a key that is overwritten with SET without KEEPTTL, so refreshing a cached value silently makes it permanent.
react-hook-form registers inputs as uncontrolled; calling watch on every keystroke re-renders the whole form, so use useWatch in the component that needs the value.
TanStack Query refetches on window focus by default; data that must not change while a user edits a form needs refetchOnWindowFocus turned off for that query.
TanStack Query v5 renamed cacheTime to gcTime and removed the onSuccess callback from useQuery; side effects belong in an effect or in mutation callbacks.
socket.io starts with HTTP long polling; behind a load balancer without sticky sessions the handshake fails, so enable sticky sessions or force the websocket transport.
axios rejects only for status codes that validateStatus refuses; with a custom validateStatus that accepts everything, 500 responses resolve and the error handling never runs.
dayjs parses date-only strings in local time, and plugins such as utc must be extended before use; formatting without the plugin shifts dates across time zones.
Playwright web-first assertions such as toBeVisible return a promise; a missing await lets a failing assertion pass silently.
Storybook builds with its own bundler config; path aliases from tsconfig or the Vite config must be added in the Storybook main config or stories fail to import.
pino writes logs asynchronously; a process that exits right after logging can lose the last lines unless the destination is flushed or created as synchronous.
uvicorn with --reload watches the working directory; large folders such as node_modules or virtual environments make reloads slow unless the reload directories are limited.
